It's clear to everyone that this medium is no longer about bringing art/imagination to life, and hasn't been for some time (if that's ever what it was really about to begin with - that's a different topic). Video games have become another form of marketing. I've taken a class in marketing (a required elective). It certainly didn't make me an expert, but it gave me an idea precisely how marketers regard their target market. And it's maximum clinical. The level of group psychology analysis that goes on in that field is mind boggling. What I'm getting at is there has been a concerted effort at maximizing the appeal of these games. And it's not just, "oh I think that will be cool!". For instance, look at the artstyle and gameplay of the most popular enduring games (and you can go back pretty far, too).

HALO, Diablo 3 (after some consideration, Diablo 2 belongs on this list), Overwatch, World of Warcraft (and Hearthstone, and Heroes of the Storm), League of Legends, Team Fortress 2, Borderlands, Starcraft, Warcraft, Gauntlet: Legends, pretty much any N64 Nintendo title, all those Nintendo "party games", and of course, Fortnite.

All these games (these are just the ones I could think of off the top of my head) have two things in common: art style, and gameplay. And as I said, it reaches back decades. Art style is cartoony, a caricature of the subject matter being presented. Large expressive faces, high color saturation, exaggerated animations, simple or 1-dimensional characters, a fair amount of zaniness ("STOP POKING ME", "How do I get out of this chickenshit outfit?"), and music to dull the visceral impact of an otherwise truly disturbing scene (e.g. bodies in various states of dismemberment in the Rogue's Monastery in Act 1 of D2)

On to gameplay. All these games are simply constructed, with just enough mechanical depth to keep you interested, but they remain "casual" - you can pick them up for a few minutes before whatever you have to do, then put them down pretty much whenever without worrying about losing any of your time investment. Look at some of the games that, at first glance, you wouldn't really separate from one of the items I listed. Resident Evil 2 met a lot of these criteria, but it was lacking the casual aspect (pick it up whenever, put it down whenever) as were pretty much all the old RE games. At first glance, RAGE might seem like a Borderlands clone. But it was lacking the artstyle - Borderlands was bright, colorful, cell shaded art, and RAGE was just plain looking by comparison. It might have been lacking in the zany department, too, I didn't play it much.

Everybody seems to have settled on the term "replay value", but that's a term that undermines what's really going on: it's pressing all the right buttons to keep you coming back for more. South Park did an episode on this, about mobile gaming, but it's the same shit. This is exactly what they have been trying to instill in their games, the quality that makes them as addictive as Fortnite seems to be. It's been the goal.
